title: How Big, How Many
description: From the tiniest bacterium to a giant egg — cells vary hugely. Master cell size and number to seize piece 5.

content.value: Cells range enormously in size. Most are so small you need a microscope. The smallest cells are bacteria. But the LARGEST single cell is the egg of an ostrich — big enough to see easily with your bare eyes!

SMALLEST cell   → bacterium (needs a microscope)  🔬
LARGEST cell    → ostrich egg (see it easily!)    🥚

Most cells are microscopic — far too small to see.
Size Doesn't Depend on Body Size

Here's a surprise: the size of a cell has NOTHING to do with the size of the animal. An elephant's cells are NOT bigger than a mouse's cells — the elephant simply has many MORE cells. Big animals have more cells, not bigger ones.

The number of cells in an organism can be one (unicellular) or many trillions (large multicellular). A human body contains many trillions of cells. Just like cell size, the number depends on the organism — and bigger organisms generally have more cells.
Common myth busted: bigger animals do NOT have bigger cells — they have more cells. A whale and a mouse have similar-sized cells; the whale just has vastly more of them.

Key Takeaway: Cells vary greatly in size (smallest = bacteria, largest single cell = ostrich egg) and number. Cell size does not depend on body size — larger organisms have more cells, not bigger ones.
